title: Two-Parameter Family of Nonlinear Dirac Equations With Scalar-Scalar plus Vector-Vector Interactions
authors: Avinash Khare, Fred Cooper, John F. Dawson, Avadh Saxena
abstract: We obtain exact solutions of the nonlinear Dirac equation in $1+1$ dimensions of the form $ψ(x,t) = e^{-iωt} ψ(x)$ for scalar-scalar (SS) plus vector-vector (VV) interaction with interaction Lagrangian given by $$L_{I} = \frac{g^2}{κ+1}[(\barψ ψ)^{κ+1} +\frac{1}{p} (\barψ γ_μψ\barψ γ^μ ψ)^{κ+1}]$$ where $p > 0$ but arbitrary otherwise. We look for solutions with $0 < ω< m$ where $ω, m$ are frequency and mass, respectively. We find solutions for all values of $ω$ in this range. We compute the charge $Q$ and the energy $E$ for each of the solitary wave solutions and explore the region in the ($p, κ$) parameter space in which solitary wave bound states exist (i.e., for which $E/Q < m$). We show that for all the cases while both $E$ and $Q$ depend on the coupling constant $g$, their ratio $E/Q$ is independent of $g$. We further find that in case $pκ\le 1$, the charge density for all the solitary waves have only single hump while for $p κ> 1$ there is a transition from double to single hump and we determine it as a function of $ω/m$. We notice that for all $p$ there is a transition at $κ=2$ in the behavior of $E/Q$ as a function of $ω$ which we speculate is related to the onset of instability of the solutions at $κ=2$. We obtain the nonrelativistic reduction of the two-parameter family to a non-relativistic modified nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) and discuss the stability of the single hump olitary waves in the domain of validity of the modified NLSE.
summary: This theoretical paper derives exact solitary wave solutions for a nonlinear Dirac equation featuring combined scalar-scalar and vector-vector interactions. Key findings include the independence of the energy-to-charge ratio from the coupling strength and a detailed analysis of how the wave profile transitions between single and double humps based on system parameters. The work concludes by examining the stability of these solutions in the non-relativistic limit.
main_problem: The paper aims to find exact solutions for a two-parameter family of nonlinear Dirac equations incorporating both scalar-scalar (SS) and vector-vector (VV) interactions.
main_result: The ratio of energy to charge ($E/Q$) for the solitary wave solutions is found to be independent of the coupling constant $g$, and the existence of bound states is analyzed based on this ratio.
method: The methodology involves seeking stationary solitary wave solutions ($\psi(x,t) = e^{-i\omega t} \psi(x)$) and analyzing the resulting conserved quantities (Energy $E$ and Charge $Q$).
model_or_system: The model is a Nonlinear Dirac Equation (NLDE) with an interaction Lagrangian $L_I$ containing terms proportional to $( ar{\psi}\psi)^{\kappa+1}$ (SS) and $( ar{\psi}\gamma_\mu\psi  ar{\psi}\gamma_\mu\psi)^{\kappa+1}$ (VV).
key_observables: Charge ($Q$), Energy ($E$), and the ratio $E/Q$, which determines the existence of bound states ($E/Q < m$).
important_parameters: The nonlinearity parameter $\kappa$, the interaction parameter $p$, the frequency $\omega$, and the mass $m$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of stationary solutions of the form $\psi(x, t) = e^{-i\omega t} \psi(x)$, and later, a non-relativistic approximation is used for stability analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition between double and single hump solitary wave profiles based on $\kappa p$, and plot the $E/Q$ ratio versus $\omega$ for various parameter choices.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of deriving the solutions, analyzing their properties (including $E/Q$ and hump shape), and concluding with a non-relativistic reduction to a modified NLSE to discuss stability.
why_interesting: The study of nonlinear wave equations, particularly those derived from Dirac equations, is fundamental in quantum field theory and condensed matter physics, providing insights into stable localized structures (solitons).
